Valley Point and Fraser Suites Singapore to be redeveloped into luxury mixed-use riverfront project
article:
Frasers Property and Mitsubishi Estate will redevelop Valley Point and Fraser Suites Singapore on River Valley Road into a luxury 999-year mixed-use project along the Singapore River.

The two firms have formed a 51:49 joint venture to undertake the redevelopment, they announced in a Sept 30 joint release.

The new development will have around 407 luxury homes and sky villas, a new flagship 184-unit Fraser Suites serviced residence, as well as dining, retail and lifestyle offerings.

The prime District 10 project is slated to launch for sale in 2027 and complete in 2031.

Both Valley Point and Fraser Suites Singapore are expected to cease operations on March 31, 2027.

Valley Point comprises a 20-storey office tower and a two-storey shopping centre, while Fraser Suites Singapore is a 255-key serviced residence.

The 13,439 sq m (144,656 sq ft) site has a maximum allowable gross floor area of 54,309 sq m (584,577 sq ft), and is zoned for commercial and residential use.

"We aim to create a distinctive riverfront destination with curated living, hospitality and lifestyle offerings," said Soon Su Lin, CEO of Frasers Property Singapore.

"We look forward to working, once again, with Mitsubishi Estate to launch this landmark project next year, building on our successful partnership on the Kallang Close government land sale site," she added.

A joint venture between the two companies in April clinched the Kallang Close land plot with the top bid of $610.75 million , or $1,415 psf per plot ratio. The 123,320 sq ft, 99-year leasehold site can yield about 470 homes.

Kato Shinya, managing director of Mitsubishi Estate Asia, described the Valley Point and Fraser Suites project as a "rare riverfront redevelopment opportunity" and said the partners will bring together their complementary strengths and shared vision for quality placemaking.

In June, Frasers Property had said it may redevelop the site after restructuring some $2.1 billion of hospitality assets, which included consolidating full ownership of Fraser Suites Singapore.

The group on Sept 30 said the site "holds a unique place" in its heritage and the history of the River Valley area.

It was once home to Fraser & Neave's first aerated water canning facility in Southeast Asia. In 1998, it housed the first Frasers Hospitality serviced residence for extended stay.

title: Skylink to issue two-year non-convertible bonds of up to $5 mil at 8% coupon rate
article:
Skylink holdings Limited (Skylink) (SGX:XZB ) announced that it will be issuing of up to $5 million of a two-year hire purchase bonds with annual coupon rate of 8%, which are payable on a half-yearly basis.

Skylink explains that the issuance will further support its credit business segment, which provides hire purchase financing solutions to customers for new and second-hand commercial vehicles, including refinancing requirements.

The company states that the net proceeds raised from this bond issuance will be used to originate additional hire purchase loan books and expand such income-generating portfolios, which may include strategic growth plans that are capable of enhancing its credit business ecosystem.

“We will continue to support the hire purchase financing needs of our SME customers, being part of our integrated commercial vehicle business ecosystem,” says Wesley Shen executive director and CEO of Skylink.

“As we continue to scale our credit business, the non-dilutive hire purchase bond provides a balanced funding structure and financial runway to further grow our hire purchase loan books from the current base of $66.24 million,” adds Teh Wing Kwan, non-independent non-executive chairman of Skylink.

Shares of Skylink closed 0.1 cent higher, or up 0.51% at 19.9 cents on Sept 30.

title: RBI’s short dollar book surges past US$200 bil on forex plan
article:
(Sept 30): The Reserve Bank of India’s net short dollar book rose past US$200 billion (RM815.9 billion) for the first time, reflecting surging future repayment obligations from a dollar diaspora programme to support the rupee.

The positions increased by US$63.3 billion to US$200.1 billion in August, largely driven by an increase in contracts maturing more than a year from now, Bloomberg calculations from the RBI data show. Short positions in that maturity rose to US$176.6 billion from US$91.5 billion, the data showed.

The US$133 billion of inflows from the diaspora deposits have bolstered the country’s foreign-exchange reserves, will help keep the balance of payments in surplus after two years of deficits and give the central bank greater firepower to support the rupee after it plunged to a series of record lows in May. The RBI has already stepped up intervention, with the latest data showing reserves fell by the most in almost two years as it sought to support the currency.

The inflows have also increased liquidity in the banking system, with excess cash surging to as high as 11 trillion rupees (RM468.2 billion) earlier this month. The RBI has been conducting sell/buy swaps in the secondary market to drain cash, which also helps in lowering its short book. The tenor of up to one month has flipped to a net loss of US$12.12 billion from a short book of US$13.2 billion in July, the data showed.

“One thing the RBI has been reportedly trying is to prematurely unwind the maturities that were due around next year,” said Abhishek Upadhyay, an economist at ICICI Securities Primary Dealership Ltd. That would help soak up excess cash, though it’s still small compared with the overall forward book, he said.

The central bank will have to repay these dollars once the deposits mature in three to five years. The record-breaking diaspora fundraising drive may prove costly for the country’s central bank, leaving it with a potential US$10.6 billion price tag, according to economists.

title: GKE buys back warehouse from ESR-REIT for $32 mil
article:
Logistics firm GKE Corp has bought back a warehouse from ESR-REIT for $32 million.

GKE, back in 2016, sold the same property to then Viva Industrial Trust for $45 million under a sale and leaseback arrangement.

All this while, GKE has been operating the property, which is at 30 Pioneer Road.

The property, which has a gross floor area of 26,1134 sqm, has a remaining lease of 10.6 years.

GKE says the acquisition will help reduce its rental obligation ahead of the end of the lease from JTC.

The property is carried on ESR-REIT's books at $32 million, the transacted price, and thus deemed by GKE as "fair and reasonable".

With this sale, ESR-REIT's portfolio will consist of 66 properties located in Singapore, Japan and Australia, as well as investments in three property funds in Australia.

ESR-REIT units closed at $2.08, down 0.48%, extending a drop of 23.81% year to date.

GKE Corp shares closed at 6.3 cents. It is down 37% year to date.

title: India hospital stocks erase US$2.6 bil as top court flags drug markup
article:
(Sept 30): Indian healthcare stocks eroded 248 billion rupees in market value on concerns that high-margin pharmacy revenue may come under threat after the top court questioned steep markups on lifesaving cancer drugs.

All but one of 17 members of the BSE Hospitals Index closed lower on Wednesday, with the gauge falling 5%. Top hospital chain Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Ltd slumped 5.7%, while Fortis Healthcare Ltd dropped 6.3% and Max Healthcare Institute Ltd fell 5.3% in Mumbai.

India’s Supreme Court asked the federal government to probe allegations that hospitals make patients purchase medicines from their own or designated pharmacies, especially when the drugs carry a steep margin, the Press Trust of India reported. A markup of as much as 10 times on cancer drugs is "carnage". PTI quoted the court as saying, asking whether there should be a uniform 16% margin on all medicines.

The scrutiny could affect large private hospitals, where medicines and ancillary services form a key component of revenues. Any move to cap margins for drugs or roll out policies preventing compulsory in-house pharmacy purchases could hit these firms.

This looks like more of a sentiment impact as these are court proceedings, and nothing has been finalised, Deepika Murarka, analyst at Choice Equity Broking Pvt, told Bloomberg News. Any price limit could impact high-margin pharmacy revenues of a few large players, including Apollo and Max, she said.

title: ISOTeam wins new contracts worth $30.2 mil
article:
ISOTeam has won new contracts worth a total of $30.2 million. Together with a variation order, its total book has now reached $179.1 million, to be delivered over the coming two to three years.

"We are pleased to begin FY2027 on a strong note with $30.2 million in new contracts secured," says group executive director and CEO Anthony Koh.

"These wins reflect the trust that our public and private sector customers place in ISOTeam, as well as the strength of our execution track record," he says.

The operating environment remains "supportive", says Koh, citing official projections of $47 billion and $53 billion in project awards for 2026.

"We will continue to actively pursue new tenders and position ourselves to capture the growth ahead,” says Koh. ISOTeam shares closed at 6.1 cents.
